clue.text: Church music composed by sincere church worker

parts.note: sincere means plain, straightforward and honest
the ant is the crossword's stock worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A piece of sacred music written by a devout verger or sexton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like an anagram signal, but here 'composed by' only joins the definition to the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong, the unaccompanied chant of the medieval liturgy, is sung in services, so it is a kind of sacred music.

clue.text: A woman put down about five hundred

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to put something down is to lay it
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone sets a woman down near a sum of five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a polite word for a woman.

clue.text: State ten was two-thirds

parts.note: ten written in figures, 10, looks like the letters I and O

indicators.note: two-thirds of a three-letter word means its first two letters are kept

explanation.surface: Someone says a state once had a population or score of ten, two-thirds of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds' keeps the first two of the three letters of 'was', giving WA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: He'll take the lead-but not on his own

definitions.text: He'll take the lead-but not on his own

parts.words: He'll take the lead-but not on his own
parts.note: an actor playing a leading role who shares top billing with another performer

explanation.surface: A would-be leader who never acts alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor sharing star billing with another takes a leading part jointly, never singly.

clue.text: Converts sat in a gathering, by no means from choice

indicators.note: converts is read as a verb: the letters of the following words are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Religious converts sat in at a meeting, though they did not really want to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converts' looks like a noun naming the people sitting in, but it is the verb signalling the anagram of SAT IN A GATHERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something reluctantly, contrary to one's natural inclination, is the idiom of going counter to the wood's fibres.

clue.text: 13 across could be such a twister!

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. ... was the great English landscape artist, so a member of 13 across's profession could be one
one who turns or twists things, such as a lathe operator

explanation.surface: A painter is said to be a real twister.
explanation.definitionFit: Turner the landscape artist is an example of the profession; literally, one who turns is something that twists.

clue.text: Prepare an old fellow for great conflict

parts.note: to arm is to prepare for fighting
aged means old
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Get an elderly man ready for a big war.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final battle of the Bible's Revelation, hence any huge, catastrophic conflict.

clue.text: Lines right for the river

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a set of lines of verse

explanation.surface: Verses with the correct river named in them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a major central European river forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Reckless men speed crazily on bad roads

indicators.note: crazily means the letters of the word before are scrambled
bad here means the letters of the following word are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild drivers race at speed along poor roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazily' turns SPEED into DESPE and 'bad' turns ROADS into RADOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperadoes are bold, reckless outlaws ready for any violence.

clue.text: An exchange of words isn't a solution for the Lower House!

indicators.note: an exchange swaps things around, here the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A debate in Parliament's Commons, an exchange of words that solves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower House' wants to be the House of Commons, but it means the lower floor of a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground floor, where servants once worked, is the lower part of a house.

clue.text: Like the individual with a large area of land

parts.note: like means as, in 'do as I do'
I is the word an individual uses for themself

explanation.surface: Like one person holding a large tract of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a vast landmass.

clue.text: A restrictive practice that won't attract customers

definitions.meaning: a workplace where only union members may be employed
a store with its doors shut gets no shoppers

explanation.definitionFit: A union-only workplace is a classic restrictive labour practice; literally, a store that is not open has no buyers.

clue.text: A person colouring rope

definitions.meaning: someone who applies colour, as an artist or decorator does
a line attached to a boat's bow for tying it up

explanation.definitionFit: An artist or decorator applies colour; sailors also use the word for the mooring line on a small boat's bow.

clue.text: Chaucer's hen not fully occupied?

definitions.meaning: Dame ..., Chanticleer's favourite hen in The Nun's Priest's Tale
read as two words, a building in part rented out

explanation.definitionFit: The hen of Chaucer's tale bears this name; split, it describes premises only partly let to tenants.

clue.text: Walker may well be up the pole!

definitions.meaning: someone who walks in the countryside for pleasure

definitions.text: may well be up the pole
definitions.meaning: a climbing rose often trained to grow up a pole or pillar

explanation.definitionFit: A hiker out for pleasure is called this; so is a climbing rose, which grows up a support.

clue.text: Find room for a vehicle about 45 inches long

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
an ell is an old English measure of length, 45 inches

explanation.surface: Make space for a car that is nearly four feet long.
explanation.walkthrough: The ell is an old cloth measure, in England 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is an underground room, usually for storage.

clue.text: Pledge to invest money by and by in solid fuel

indicators.note: in puts the money and the by-and-by pieces inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
by and by means later, in due course

explanation.surface: A promise to put money, eventually, into coal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' suggests finance, but here 'in' is the container signal; 'money' is L because the pound sign comes from libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is security pledged against a loan.

clue.text: There's competition, note, to raise such a flower

parts.note: a race is a competition
ME is a variant spelling of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Gardeners compete to grow a particular bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a flower cluster with flowers on short stalks along a central stem, as in a foxglove.

clue.text: A right heel!

parts.note: read as nautical terms: a ship leaning over towards its right-hand side

explanation.surface: A thoroughly bad man, really a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A right heel' sounds like an insult for a cad, but heel means a ship's lean and right means the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship heels when it leans, and its right side is starboard, so the phrase describes leaning that way.

clue.text: A man of the cloth went first, and that's not good

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a clergyman's degree
led means went first, at the front

explanation.surface: A clergyman took the lead, and that was bad news.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled eggs are rotten, and an addled mind is muddled, so either way the sense is spoilt.

clue.text: Bores the doctor with complaints

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
ills are ailments, complaints

explanation.surface: A doctor's patients drone on about their ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' wants to be people who tire you, but it is the verb meaning makes holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill is to bore a hole.

clue.text: Come back and enlist again

definitions.meaning: to sign up once more, as with a regiment

explanation.definitionFit: To retort is to answer back; to sign up again is literally to join anew.

clue.text: Spread about no more

parts.note: RE means about, concerning
past means gone, no more

explanation.surface: A feast that is gone and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a lavish meal, as is a repast.

clue.text: Pressed for a letting off

parts.note: read as the part of a gun squeezed to fire it, not someone begging to be excused

explanation.surface: Someone urged to grant a pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letting off' suggests excusing someone, but here it is firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's catch is squeezed to fire it, letting off the shot.

clue.text: Repeat a section of the chorus

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sing part of the chorus again.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to repeat a sound or words.

clue.text: Make a move to supply porridge

definitions.meaning: to move slightly, as in to rouse oneself
British slang for a prison sentence, and so for prison itself

explanation.walkthrough: Doing porridge is British slang for serving time in prison, and stir is also slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to make a small move; as slang, both words mean jail time.

clue.text: A number may be attached to any wild bird

indicators.note: attached to puts the number piece alongside the next one, in front

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: wild says the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A number may be fixed to any wild bird, as with ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a talkative Asian starling, kept for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Appeals with an attempt to make a joke of it

parts.note: pleas are appeals
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Begging and trying to laugh the matter off.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light, jocular remark.

clue.text: Venomous creatures quietly getting in dope

indicators.note: getting in says the quiet piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
P, piano, is the music direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Poisonous snakes silently slipping into the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, as in Cleopatra's story.

clue.text: Playing a role isn't a requirement of a politician

indicators.note: playing with the letters of the following words rearranges them

explanation.surface: Acting a part is not something a politician needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks like acting a role, but it signals rearranging A ROLE ISN'T A.
explanation.definitionFit: Senatorial means relating to a senator, a type of legislator.
